claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine whether you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess this properly, I'll need to gather some information about you and your children.

Let me start with a basic question:

**How many children are you inquiring about, and what are their names?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I'm inquiring about my child, Alex. Just wondering if I can claim Child Benefit for them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're inquiring about **Alex**. 

Before I can assess your eligibility, I need to gather some details. Let me start with the first question:

**What is Alex's date of birth?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex just turned 16 recently - their birthday was a few months ago.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that information. I need to check the specific eligibility rules to ensure I'm asking the right questions. Let me do that now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. Since Alex is now 16, there are additional eligibility criteria I need to check. According to the rules, you can continue to claim Child Benefit for a 16-year-old if they're in approved education or training.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, are they in school, sixth form, college, or an apprenticeship?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, Alex actually left school recently, but they've just registered with the local careers service to figure out what they want to do next.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful to know. Based on the information you've provided, Alex has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service. Let me check the specific rules about this situation to make sure I have all the details correct.

Before I make my assessment, I have one more question:

**How long ago did Alex register with the careers service?** (I need to know this because there are specific time limits that apply in this situation.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It was quite recent - just a few weeks ago, actually.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on the eligibility rules I've reviewed:

**You can continue to claim Child Benefit for Alex for up to 20 weeks** after they left education or training, as long as they're registered with a government-sponsored careers service. Since Alex only registered with the careers service a few weeks ago, you're well within that 20-week window.

However, I need to confirm one final detail to complete my assessment:

**Are you the person who is responsible for Alex and lives with them in the UK?** (Or are you paying at least the equivalent of Child Benefit towards their care, such as food, clothes, or pocket money?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me here in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect, thank you for confirming that. I now have all the information I need to make my assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great news! **You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:

- **Alex is 16 years old** and has left education, but the rules allow you to continue claiming for a 16 or 17-year-old for up to **20 weeks** after they leave education or training, as long as they register with a government-sponsored careers service.
- **Alex has registered with the local careers service**, which qualifies them for this extended eligibility period.
- **Since the registration was only a few weeks ago**, Alex is well within that 20-week window.
- **You live in the UK and are responsible for Alex**, which meets the core requirement for Child Benefit eligibility.

You should be able to apply for Child Benefit for Alex. Just keep in mind that the 20-week period is limited, so if Alex doesn't return to approved education or training within that time, eligibility will end after the 20 weeks have passed.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
